newsitem.title: USA: NYS lawmakers face hurdles with school bond - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYS lawmakers face hurdles with school bond - paper.

text.p: New York State lawmakers are weighing a five-year, $2 billion borrowing plan to build or repair schools, but the proposal, put forward by Assembly Democrats, faces hurdles, the New York Times said Wednesday.

The plan is tied to budget talks, which are deadlocked although the state's budget was due on April 1. While the paper said there is broad political support for the school bond plan, the legislature must approve it by August 4 in order to get it placed on the ballot this November.
Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, told the Times: "I don't see the governor making any movement toward finishing things by August 4." He is the main architect of the bond act plan.

But Republican officials said the plan was still alive. The paper quoted a Pataki spokesman as saying: "We're willing to talk about any and all proposals." The Senate Majority Leader, Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, referring to the school bond act, said: "It's possible."
If approved by the voters, the plan would authorize the first bond act in the state's history devoted solely to renovating schools, education officials told the paper.

The Assembly's plan, which likely would be modified by Pataki and the Republican-led Senate, calls for the state to borrow $400 million to $600 million a year over the next five years to relieve overcrowding, correct school safety problems and replace old buildings.
The state now spends almost $700 million a year on school construction and maintenance, the Times said.
